what_this_is: The MEASURED hours per 110 training runs per fit, per model, on QM9. The generator sized every wall from a per-model GUESS before this file existed; fourteen of nineteen guesses were over by more than 5x and the worst by 190x, while the ONE guess that was accurate (qrf) is the one model about to be killed at its wall -- because a 1.25x margin on an accurate estimate is thinner than a 1.25x margin on a 10x overestimate.
the_margin_why: One margin cannot cover three qualities of evidence. A rate from enough finished tasks that the slowest in the array has probably been seen gets 2.0x. A rate from a task that had NOT finished, or from too few of the array, is a LOWER BOUND and gets 3.0x plus a floor built from that model's own laptop timing divided by the smallest speed-up ARC has ever shown -- doubling a floor is not a margin. No ARC rate at all gets the laptop number at 2.5x. The generator names the grade of every wall it writes, every run. See slurm_scripts_qm9_rerun/generate_scripts.py, beside WALL_MARGIN.
how_to_update: Re-run scripts/measure_walls.py on the cluster and raise any model whose longest observed task now exceeds measured_task_hours. Never lower one below what has been observed. Fill completed_tasks, tasks_in_the_measured_array and still_running as well -- a model moves from a lower bound to a measurement when its own array does, and nothing in the generator has to be edited for that.

gauche_rbf.measured_on: QM9 main grid 12980590, sacct 2026-09-07 07:20, all 18 tasks. A task is 7 noise levels x 9 replicates = 63 training runs.
gauche_rbf.provenance: CORRECTED 2026-09-07 by chat 2. The old rate of 0.4559 was this same task time divided by 6 fits, and the tasks it was read from did ONE fit each: the out-of-fold pass threw at the guard before doing any of its extra fits (RERUN_PLAN.md 13.27 D2). 0.4559 x 6 = 2.7354 against 2.7132 measured directly, which is the same number twice. All 18 tasks now agree on it: the 9 that failed on the Gaussian-process cap ran 56:29 to 1:32:29 and the 7 that completed without an out-of-fold pass ran 43:55 to 1:33:14, and both groups did one fit per training run. The rate here is 110 training runs at ONE fit, which is the accounting wall_hours() applies its own fit count to.
gauche_rbf.still_a_lower_bound_why: 7 completed of 18 is under the generator's half-the-array rule, so this stays graded `partial` and the wall is still priced from the laptop floor. Nothing has yet measured this model WITH the out-of-fold pass working, and that is the expensive path -- so the margin is doing real work and must not be cut on arithmetic. One resubmitted ECFP4, PDV or ChemBERTa task finishing under c223ec3 settles it.
gauche_rbf.do_not_use_the_laptop_row_as_a_floor: results/tuning_local/timing.csv times gauche_rbf on ECFP4 at 11,695.3 s for one fit on 8,000 molecules, written 2026-08-27T21:29:13. GP_DEFAULTS' one-thread setting was still TRUE then and was set FALSE on 2026-08-28, so that row is a single-threaded fit and ARC runs it on eight cores. ARC does the same fit at the 5,000 cap in about 88 seconds against the laptop's rescaled 2,855. That 32x is a threading difference, not a machine speed-up, so the laptop row is not a valid upper bound on the ARC rate for THIS model. Re-time it on this laptop with the current setting before using it as a floor again.
gauche_rbf.the_out_of_fold_pass_is_measured_2026_09: Screen array 12971618, a task of 7 training runs. The three tasks WITHOUT the pass (MHG-GNN 14:32, Avalon 12:22, Sort & Slice 12:23) give a startup cost of 164 s against the main grid's 88.8 s per training run at one fit. The two WITH it (ECFP4 28:39, PDV 28:58) then give 223.5 s per training run, which is 2.52x one fit -- not the 3.56x the cubic arithmetic predicts, and far under the six FULL fits wall_hours() prices. A main-grid task is 3.96 h and a deep-run task 4.39 h. The rate above stays the ONE-FIT rate because that is what wall_hours() applies its own fit count to; this note is here so nobody re-derives it.

mlp_bnn_full_mve.provenance: completed, 7 of 18. Under half the array, so the slowest task in it has probably not been seen and the generator grades this a lower bound. Its table entry is DERIVED (1.5x mlp_bnn_full), not a timing row of this model, so there is no laptop floor to put under it and the wall is 3.0x the bound. Its sibling dnn_bnn_full_mve finished 14 of 18 and is graded a measurement.

the_three_new_fields: completed_tasks, tasks_in_the_measured_array and still_running are what the generator reads to grade a rate. Before 2026-09-07 that information existed only as prose inside `provenance` -- 'STILL RUNNING, not finished', 'completed, 4 -- the rest failed on the GP bug' -- which no program could act on, so a rate from 4 tasks of 18 was trusted exactly as far as a rate from 15. The array size is the QM9 main grid's own: 3 conditions x 6 representations = 18 tasks, and 3 for gauche, which runs on ECFP4 alone. ngboost's completed_tasks is 0 because its rate comes from the one task still running. A model whose entry LACKS these fields is graded a lower bound, never measured.
